overview: Carrefour is a French multinational food retailer operating hypermarkets, supermarkets, convenience stores, cash-and-carry outlets and e-commerce across a multi-format, omni-channel network of roughly 15,700 stores in 40 countries, with direct operations now concentrated in France, Spain, Belgium, Poland, Brazil and Argentina (Romania and Italy sold/sold-in-progress, Turkey agreed for sale in 2026). France is the core market (roughly 40% of sales), with Brazil (via Atacadão cash-and-carry, now a wholly-owned subsidiary) the largest international market. The group is mid-way through a portfolio simplification ('Carrefour 2026'/'Carrefour 2030' plans) that has pared non-core geographies to focus capital on France, Spain and Brazil.

business_model.summary: Carrefour generates revenue primarily through retail sale of food and non-food goods across multiple store formats (hypermarkets, supermarkets, convenience, cash & carry), supplemented by e-commerce/marketplace GMV, a financial-services/banking arm (Carrefour Banque, consumer credit and insurance), real-estate/retail-media monetization, and franchise fees. Own-brand penetration (38% of net sales in 2025, targeting 40% by 2026) is central to margin and differentiation strategy. Revenue is overwhelmingly transactional/recurring (everyday grocery spend) rather than project-based, with modest subscription/loyalty-driven recurring revenue (Le Club Carrefour ~14.7m members in France; El Club Carrefour/PASS in Spain ~10.8m members).

revenue_streams.name: Financial services, real estate, retail media

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market grocery and general merchandise, with a cash-and-carry wholesale component (Atacadão) serving small retailers/foodservice (B2B) alongside individual consumers
business_model.geographic_mix: France ~41%, Brazil ~18%, Spain ~10%, Other countries (Belgium, Poland, Argentina) ~9%, with Italy, Romania and Turkey being divested/held for sale (together historically ~10-12% of group sales)

competitive_position.market_position: Second-largest grocery retailer in France by market share (~21.1% vs. E.Leclerc's ~24.9% as of late 2025, per Worldpanel/Kantar data), and the largest hypermarket/cash-and-carry operator in Brazil through Atacadão following the 2025 minority buyout.

moat_factors.description: Large store network and own-brand sourcing give bargaining leverage with suppliers, though French price wars with discounters erode the benefit
38% of net sales from Carrefour-brand products supports margin and price perception versus national brands
~15,700 stores across hypermarket, supermarket, convenience and cash & carry formats provide channel flexibility and proximity, but also costly format overlap
Le Club Carrefour (14.7m members, France) and El Club/PASS (10.8m, Spain) enable personalization and growing retail-media monetization (Unlimitail JV with Publicis)
Atacadão is the leading discount/cash-and-carry format in Brazil, now wholly owned, benefiting from continued store expansion and share gains

weaknesses: Structurally lower margins and persistent share losses to E.Leclerc and hard discounters (Lidl) in the core French hypermarket format
Heavy reliance on low-margin, capital-intensive hypermarkets facing secular format decline versus convenience and discount
Complex, sprawling multi-country portfolio historically diluted management focus and capital allocation (now being unwound via Italy/Romania/Turkey exits)
High exposure to volatile, inflation-prone Latin American currencies (BRL, ARS) that create earnings and balance-sheet noise
Thin net margins (sub-1% net margin in several recent years) leave limited buffer against cost shocks or one-off disruptions

growth_drivers: Portfolio simplification refocusing capital and management on three core markets (France, Spain, Brazil) after exiting Italy, Romania and Turkey
Atacadão/cash-and-carry expansion in Brazil (target of 470+ stores by 2026) continuing to take share in a structurally growing discount channel
E-commerce and omni-channel growth (GMV +21% in 2025; group target of €10bn GMV by 2026), including marketplace expansion and partnerships (UberEats, Deliveroo, Mercado Livre)
Convenience-format expansion (600+ stores/year since 2022) capturing share from traditional hypermarkets and addressing urban proximity demand
Own-brand mix shift toward 40% of food sales, supporting gross margin and price competitiveness
Retail media and data monetization via the Unlimitail joint venture with Publicis, a high-margin, capital-light revenue stream
Cost-savings program targeting €1.0bn in savings for 2026 (part of a cumulative €4.2bn target since 2022) and continued synergy capture from the Cora/Match integration (€130m targeted by 2027)
Real estate value realization (sale-and-leaseback, mixed-use development in France, large private property company in Brazil)

business.description: E.Leclerc continues to gain share; discounters (Lidl) and hard-discount-format expansion by rivals pressure Carrefour's hypermarket economics

business.risk: Format mix exposure to structurally declining hypermarkets
business.description: Large-box hypermarket format continues to lose relative share to convenience, online and discount channels

business.risk: Integration/execution risk on Cora and Match
business.description: Despite ADLC approval and store conversions completed in 2025, full synergy capture (€130m by 2027) and restructuring (GEPP plan announced May 2026) still in progress
Simultaneous divestitures (Italy, Romania, Turkey) alongside the Brazil Atacadão full-ownership integration create management and operational complexity

financial.description: Net debt rose from €3.97bn (Dec 2025) to €5.85bn (June 2026) on seasonal and refinancing effects; total borrowings ~€11.1bn against thin net margins

financial.risk: Brazilian real / Argentine peso currency and hyperinflation exposure
financial.description: Argentina is accounted for under IAS 29 hyperinflation rules; BRL/ARS swings materially distort reported growth and equity (FX appreciation added ~€0.5-0.8bn to equity in H1 2026 alone)
H1 2026 effective tax rate of 55% driven by France's special 41.2% large-company surtax and non-recognition of deferred tax assets in Brazil

regulatory.description: ADLC required divestiture of nine stores as a condition of the Cora/Match acquisition approval (completed July 2025)
Ongoing political pressure in France over retailer-supplier margin sharing and agricultural pricing could constrain pricing flexibility

regulatory.risk: Cross-border regulatory approval risk on pending divestitures
regulatory.description: Romania (Paval Holding) and Turkey (Turgut Aydin Holdings) sales remain subject to regulatory approvals and could be delayed or renegotiated

macro.description: October 2026 riots/looting directly damaged roughly 50 stores on the first day, forced precautionary closures and curfew-related reduced hours across ~6,000 French stores, with management estimating an €80-200m operating income hit and reduced Q4 footfall during peak shopping season
Poland faces food deflation since June 2026 and weak consumer confidence; Argentina and Brazil consumers face ongoing purchasing-power pressure despite volume gains

macro.risk: Interest rate and financing cost exposure
macro.description: Significant bond/lease-related debt load means financing costs are sensitive to rate moves, partly mitigated by 2025 refinancing of Atacadão's Brazilian debt into lower-cost euro debt

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Mature, low-single-digit-growth European grocery market with structural channel shift toward discount, convenience and online (online grocery projected to grow ~8.6%/year 2022-2027 vs. 3.7% offline); Latin American grocery (Brazil, Argentina) offers higher nominal growth but with currency/inflation volatility
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate - grocery retail is largely non-discretionary and defensive, but discretionary non-food categories, consumer purchasing power and now acute social/political disruption in France add volatility
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - meaningful bond and lease-related debt load (~€11bn borrowings) makes refinancing costs rate-sensitive, though recent refinancing of Brazilian debt into euro-denominated debt reduced the cost of net debt
key_input_costs: Food commodity costs (passed through to consumers to varying degrees)
Energy costs for store operations and logistics
Labor costs in France and Europe
Fuel/petrol costs affecting reported gross sales growth

recent_developments.event: Carrefour cut FY2026 guidance (operating margin growth, adjusted EPS, net free cash flow) citing social unrest and security deterioration in France; stock fell ~14.7% intraday to roughly EUR13.91, with Morgan Stanley downgrading to equal-weight (target cut to EUR18.35) and Oddo BHF cutting target to EUR14.00

Management disclosed that French riots/looting damaged roughly 50 stores on the first day and forced precautionary closures/curfew-driven reduced hours across much of its ~6,000-store French network; CFO estimated an EUR80-200m hit to operating income and warned of reduced Q4 footfall

Q3 2026 trading update showed +2.3% group like-for-like sales (France +1.2%, Spain +2.1%, Brazil +1.4%, Argentina +24.2% on hyperinflation accounting), e-commerce GMV +15-18%, broadly in line with H1 trends before the guidance cut
Completed sale of Carrefour Romania to Paval Holding (enterprise value ~EUR820-823m), reclassified as discontinued operations
Agreed to sell 89% stake in Turkish unit CarrefourSA to Turgut Aydin Holdings, pending regulatory approval, continuing the non-core market exit strategy

Announced an Employment and Career Management Plan (GEPP) restructuring for French subsidiary Cora stores, plus restructuring measures in Spain and Argentina, generating non-recurring charges in H1 2026

Agreed to sell the entire Italian business (1,188 stores, ~EUR4.2bn 2024 gross sales) to NewPrinces Group at an enterprise value of ~EUR1bn, after years of negative recurring operating income and negative free cash flow in Italy

Completed buyout of minority shareholders in Carrefour Brasil/Atacadão via a merger structure at BRL8.50/share (or Carrefour SA shares/BDRs), taking the Brazilian subsidiary fully private and delisting it from B3; issued ~58.3m new Carrefour shares as part of the exchange
Refinanced Atacadão's external Brazilian debt with euro-denominated debt issued by Carrefour SA at materially more favorable rates, reducing the cost of net debt
French competition authority (ADLC) gave final approval for the Cora/Match acquisition integration; nine stores subsequently divested per ADLC remedies (completed July 2025)

items.notes: Cut from +25bps guided in February 2026, due to French social/security disruption
Cut from high single-digit growth guided in February 2026
Cut from slight growth guided in February 2026; comparison base is 2025 pro forma excluding Italy (EUR1,565m)
Reduced from EUR1.7bn guided in February 2026

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Alexandre Bompard said roughly 50 stores were hit by looting on the first day of unrest in France and the damage was considerable; CFO Matthieu Malige estimated a total operating income impact of EUR80-200m from store damage, closures and curfews, and flagged reduced customer footfall heading into the critical Q4 year-end shopping period, calling it 'a new situation marked by deep uncertainty.' Management maintained that underlying commercial momentum (Q3 LFL +2.3%, in line with H1 and prior expectations) remained solid in France, Spain and Brazil absent the unrest impact.

bull_case: Portfolio simplification (Italy, Romania, Turkey exits; full Brazil ownership) sharpens focus on three higher-quality core markets and should improve consolidated margins and cash conversion over time
Atacadão's continued expansion and share gains in Brazil provide a structural growth engine now fully consolidated without minority dilution
Cost-savings program (EUR1.0bn targeted for 2026, cumulative EUR4.2bn since 2022) and Cora/Match synergies (EUR130m by 2027) offer a credible self-help margin lever independent of top-line trends
Growing e-commerce (+21% in 2025) and retail-media/Unlimitail monetization provide higher-margin, capital-light growth alongside the core retail business

Depressed valuation after the October 2026 selloff (~8x earnings pre-cut, shares near multi-year lows) may already discount much of the near-term French disruption, leaving room for recovery if unrest subsides and Q4 trading normalizes
bear_case: France remains structurally challenged: Carrefour continues to lose share to E.Leclerc and discounters, and the October 2026 social unrest/security crisis has materially cut FY2026 guidance (EPS, margin, free cash flow) right before the critical holiday quarter
Thin net margins (historically well under 1%) leave little cushion against cost shocks, one-off disruptions, or further guidance cuts if unrest or curfews persist

Heavy and rising leverage (net debt nearly doubled from EUR3.97bn to EUR5.85bn between Dec 2025 and June 2026) combined with a high effective tax rate (55% in H1 2026) constrains financial flexibility

Significant residual execution risk from the simultaneous Italy/Romania/Turkey divestitures, Cora/Match restructuring (GEPP plan), and Brazil integration, any of which could generate further one-off charges or distraction

Latin American currency and hyperinflation accounting (Argentina under IAS 29) add volatility and reduce the transparency/comparability of reported growth, while Poland faces food deflation and weak demand
